literal: The Four Princes of Wenxuan
idiomatic: The Four Princes of Wenxuan

literal: Prince of Taiyuan Shaode; Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi; Prince of Xihe Shaoren; Prince of Longxi Shaolian
idiomatic: Prince of Taiyuan (Shaode); Prince of Fanyang (Shaoyi); Prince of Xihe (Shaoren); Prince of Longxi (Shaolian)

literal: Wenxuan had five sons: Empress Li bore the Deposed Emperor and Prince Shaode of Taiyuan; Lady Feng bore Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang; Lady Pei bore Prince Shaoren of Xihe; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaolian of Longxi.
idiomatic: Gao Yang had five sons: Empress Li bore the Deposed Emperor and Prince Shaode of Taiyuan; Lady Feng bore Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang; Lady Pei bore Prince Shaoren of Xihe; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaolian of Longxi.

literal: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan was Wenxuan's second son.
idiomatic: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan was Gao Yang's second son.

literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he was made Opener of the Way with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, he was made opener of the way with honors equal to the three ducal ministers.

literal: Because Wucheng was enraged at Empress Li, he cursed at Shaode, saying, "When your father was beating me, you didn't come to save me!
idiomatic: Because Gao Zhan was enraged at Empress Li, he cursed at Shaode, saying, "When your father was beating me, you didn't come to save me!

literal: " He killed him by striking with the ring of his knife, and personally buried him with earth in the Pleasure Garden.
idiomatic: " He killed him by striking with the ring of his knife, and personally buried him with earth in the Pleasure Garden.

literal: In the first year of Wuping, an edict made Biancai, son of the Prince of Fanyang, his successor to inherit the title Prince of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping, an edict made Biancai, son of the Prince of Fanyang, his successor to inherit the title Prince of Taiyuan.

literal: Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang was Wenxuan's third son.
idiomatic: Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang was Gao Yang's third son.

literal: At first he was enfeoffed at Guangyang, later enfeoffed at Fanyang.
idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed at Guangyang, later enfeoffed at Fanyang.

literal: He rose in succession to Palace Attendant and Governor of Qingdu.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to palace attendant and governor of Qingdu.

literal: He liked to drink with low companions, arbitrarily appointed palace attendants, and beat to death the Erudite Ren Fangrong.
idiomatic: He liked to drink with low companions, arbitrarily appointed palace attendants, and beat to death the erudite Ren Fangrong.

literal: Wucheng once caned him two hundred strokes and sent him to Empress Zhaoxin; the empress caned him another hundred.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan once caned him two hundred strokes and sent him to Empress Zhaoxin; the empress caned him another hundred.

literal: When Houzhu fled to Ye, Shaoyi was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: When the Last Emperor fled to Ye, Shaoyi was made chief minister of the secretariat and governor of Ding Province.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou captured Bing Province, he made Feng Fuxiang Military Governor of Beishuo Province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou captured Bing Province, he made Feng Fuxiang military governor of Beishuo Province.

literal: Qi regarded this place as a strategic stronghold; many brave warriors gathered there.
idiomatic: Qi regarded this place as a strategic stronghold; many brave warriors gathered there.

literal: The former Administrator Zhao Mu, the Commander Wang Dangwan, and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome the Prince of Rencheng at Ying Province.
idiomatic: The former administrator Zhao Mu, the commander Wang Dangwan, and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome the Prince of Rencheng at Ying Province.

literal: The affair did not succeed, so they welcomed Shaoyi instead.
idiomatic: The affair did not succeed, so they welcomed Shaoyi instead.

literal: Shaoyi reached Mayi.
idiomatic: Shaoyi reached Mayi.

literal: Fuxiang and his subordinates Han A'onu and several dozen others were all Qi defectors; from Si Province northward, more than two hundred and eighty garrisons all followed Fuxiang, and when Shaoyi arrived, they all turned.
idiomatic: Fuxiang and his subordinates Han A'onu and several dozen others were all Qi defectors; from Si Province northward, more than two hundred and eighty garrisons all followed Fuxiang, and when Shaoyi arrived, they all turned.

literal: Shaoyi and Governor of Ling Province Yuan Hongmeng led troops south, intending to take Bing Province; when they reached Xinxing, Si Province was already held by Zhou.
idiomatic: Shaoyi and Governor of Ling Province Yuan Hongmeng led troops south, intending to take Bing Province; when they reached Xinxing, Si Province was already held by Zhou.

literal: The vanguard's two Military Companions of the Fourth Rank surrendered to Zhou with their commands.
idiomatic: The vanguard's two military companions of the fourth rank surrendered to Zhou with their commands.

literal: Zhou forces attacked Xian Province, captured the governor Lu Qiong, and also captured several cities.
idiomatic: Zhou forces attacked Xian Province, captured Governor Lu Qiong, and also captured several cities.

literal: Shaoyi withdrew to hold Beishuo.
idiomatic: Shaoyi withdrew to hold Beishuo.

literal: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju's army pressed Mayi; Shaoyi sent Du Mingda to resist, and the troops suffered a great defeat.
idiomatic: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju's army pressed Mayi; Shaoyi sent Du Mingda to resist, and the troops suffered a great defeat.

literal: Shaoyi said, "Death is all there is — I cannot surrender to others.
idiomatic: Shaoyi said, "Death is all there is — I cannot surrender to others.

literal: " Thereupon he fled to the Turks.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he fled to the Turks.

literal: Three thousand households followed him; he ordered them, "Whoever wishes to return may do as they please.
idiomatic: Three thousand households followed him; he ordered them, "Whoever wishes to return may do as they please.

literal: " More than half wept, bowed, and took leave.
idiomatic: " More than half wept, bowed, and took leave.

literal: The Turkic Khan Tabo, who called Wenxuan a heroic Son of Heaven, loved and valued Shaoyi because his heavy ankles resembled Wenxuan's; all Qi people in the north were placed under Shaoyi's command.
idiomatic: The Turkic khan Tabo, who called Gao Yang a heroic Son of Heaven, loved and valued Shaoyi because his heavy ankles resembled Gao Yang's; all Qi people in the north were placed under Shaoyi's command.

literal: Gao Baoning was at Ying Province and submitted a memorial with an honorific title; Shaoyi thereupon ascended the imperial throne, proclaiming the first year of Wuping.
idiomatic: Gao Baoning was at Ying Province and submitted a memorial with an honorific title; Shaoyi thereupon ascended the imperial throne, proclaiming the first year of Wuping.

literal: Zhao Mu was made Prince of Tianshui.
idiomatic: Zhao Mu was made Prince of Tianshui.

literal: Tabo heard Baoning had taken Ping Province and also summoned the various tribes, each raising troops southward, declaring they would jointly set up the Prince of Fanyang as Qi emperor and avenge him.
idiomatic: Tabo heard Baoning had taken Ping Province and also summoned the various tribes, each raising troops southward, declaring they would jointly set up the Prince of Fanyang as Qi emperor and avenge him.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou massed troops at Yunyang, intending to lead a northern campaign in person, but suddenly died of illness.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou massed troops at Yunyang, intending to lead a northern campaign in person, but suddenly died of illness.

literal: When Shaoyi heard of it, he thought Heaven was aiding him.
idiomatic: When Shaoyi heard of it, he thought Heaven was aiding him.

literal: Lu Changsi held Fanyang and also submitted a memorial welcoming Shaoyi.
idiomatic: Lu Changsi held Fanyang and also submitted a memorial welcoming Shaoyi.

literal: Before long Zhou general Yuwen Shenju attacked and destroyed Changqi.
idiomatic: Before long Zhou general Yuwen Shenju attacked and destroyed Changqi.

literal: That day Shaoyi happened to reach You Province; hearing Zhou's military governor had sent troops outward, he wished to take advantage of the vacancy to seize Ji City; he displayed the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, ascended the tomb mound of King Zhao of Yan, and from the height looked far and arrayed his troops.
idiomatic: That day Shaoyi happened to reach You Province; hearing Zhou's military governor had sent troops outward, he wished to take advantage of the vacancy to seize Ji City; he displayed the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, ascended the tomb mound of King Zhao of Yan, and from the height looked far and arrayed his troops.

literal: Shenju sent Grand General Yuwen En with four thousand men to ride to relief at You Province; half were killed by Qi troops.
idiomatic: Shenju sent Grand General Yuwen En with four thousand men to ride to relief at You Province; half were killed by Qi troops.

literal: When Shaoyi heard Fanyang had fallen, he put on plain mourning clothes and wailed; he turned his army and entered the Turks.
idiomatic: When Shaoyi heard Fanyang had fallen, he put on plain mourning clothes and wailed; he turned his army and entered the Turks.

literal: Zhou men put a price on his head with Tabo and also sent He Ruoyi to persuade him.
idiomatic: Zhou men put a price on his head with Tabo and also sent He Ruoyi to persuade him.

literal: Tabo still could not bear to do it; he feigned going hunting with Shaoyi on the southern border and had Ruoyi seize him, then exiled him to Shu.
idiomatic: Tabo still could not bear to do it; he feigned going hunting with Shaoyi on the southern border and had Ruoyi seize him, then exiled him to Shu.

literal: Shaoyi's consort, daughter of Feng Xiaowan of Bohai, escaped from the Turks and returned home.
idiomatic: Shaoyi's consort, daughter of Feng Xiaowan of Bohai, escaped from the Turks and returned home.

literal: Shaoyi in Shu sent a letter to his consort saying, "The barbarians are faithless — they sent me here.
idiomatic: Shaoyi in Shu sent a letter to his consort saying, "The barbarians are faithless — they sent me here.

literal: " At last he died in Shu.
idiomatic: " At last he died in Shu.

literal: Prince Shaoren of Xihe was Wenxuan's fourth son; at the end of Tianbao he was made Opener of the Way with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
idiomatic: Prince Shaoren of Xihe was Gao Yang's fourth son; at the end of Tianbao he was made opener of the way with honors equal to the three ducal ministers.

literal: Before long he died.
idiomatic: Before long he died.

literal: Prince Shaolian of Longxi was Wenxuan's fifth son.
idiomatic: Prince Shaolian of Longxi was Gao Yang's fifth son.

literal: At first he was enfeoffed at Changle, later the title was changed.
idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed at Changle, later the title was changed.

literal: By nature he was violent and rough; once he drew a knife and chased Shaoyi; Shaoyi ran into the stables and shut the door to keep him out.
idiomatic: By nature he was violent and rough; once he drew a knife and chased Shaoyi; Shaoyi ran into the stables and shut the door to keep him out.

literal: When Shaoyi first served as Governor of Qingdu but had not yet taken up affairs, Shaolian went ahead, summoned all prisoners out, and disposed of cases as he saw fit.
idiomatic: When Shaoyi first served as governor of Qingdu but had not yet taken up affairs, Shaolian went ahead, summoned all prisoners out, and disposed of cases as he saw fit.

literal: He could drink wine — one draft of several sheng; he ultimately died of it.
idiomatic: He could drink wine — one draft of several sheng; he ultimately died of it.

literal: The Six Princes of Xiaozhao
idiomatic: The Six Princes of Xiaozhao

literal: Prince Bainian of Leiling; Prince Yande of Shiping; Prince Yanji of Chengyang; Prince Yankang of Dingyang; Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang; Prince Yanli of Runan
idiomatic: Prince Bainian of Leiling; Prince Yande of Shiping; Prince Yanji of Chengyang; Prince Yankang of Dingyang; Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang; Prince Yanli of Runan

literal: Xiaozhao had seven sons: the Empress bore Prince Bainian of Leiling; Lady Sang bore Prince Liang of Xiangcheng — who was given in adoption to Prince Jing of Xiangcheng; various ladies bore Prince Yanli of Runan, Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang.
idiomatic: Gao Yan had seven sons: the empress bore Prince Bainian of Leiling; Lady Sang bore Prince Liang of Xiangcheng — who was given in adoption to Prince Jing of Xiangcheng; various ladies bore Prince Yanli of Runan, Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang.

literal: Prince Bainian of Leiling was Xiaozhao's second son.
idiomatic: Prince Bainian of Leiling was Gao Yan's second son.

literal: When Xiaozhao first ascended, he was at Jinyang; the court ministers requested establishing the empress and crown prince; the emperor modestly did not consent; the officials at the capital again petitioned, and only then, in the empress dowager's name, he was established as crown prince.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan first ascended, he was at Jinyang; the court ministers requested establishing the empress and crown prince; the emperor modestly did not consent; the officials at the capital again petitioned, and only then, in the empress dowager's name, he was established as crown prince.

literal: As the emperor faced death, his final edict transferred the throne to Wucheng, and included a handwritten note; at the end it read, "Bainian is without guilt — you may keep him at leisure; do not follow those who came before.
idiomatic: As the emperor faced death, his final edict transferred the throne to Gao Zhan, and included a handwritten note; at the end it read, "Bainian is without guilt — you may keep him at leisure; do not follow those who came before.

literal: " In the Daning era he was enfeoffed Prince of Leiling.
idiomatic: " In the Daning era he was enfeoffed Prince of Leiling.

literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Heqing, a white rainbow twice encircled the sun, again stretching across without reaching through.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Heqing, a white rainbow twice encircled the sun, again stretching across without reaching through.

literal: A red star appeared; the emperor used a basin of water to catch the star's reflection and cover it — in one night the basin broke by itself.
idiomatic: A red star appeared; the emperor used a basin of water to catch the star's reflection and cover it — in one night the basin broke by itself.

literal: He intended to use Bainian to suppress these omens.
idiomatic: He intended to use Bainian to suppress these omens.

literal: It happened that a man of Boling, Jia Dezao, taught Bainian writing; Bainian once wrote several characters for "edict," and Dezao sealed them and submitted the sample.
idiomatic: It happened that a man of Boling, Jia Dezao, taught Bainian writing; Bainian once wrote several characters for "edict," and Dezao sealed them and submitted the sample.

literal: The emperor thereupon flew into rage and had Bainian summoned.
idiomatic: The emperor thereupon flew into rage and had Bainian summoned.

literal: When Bainian was summoned, knowing he could not escape, he cut off his belt-girdle and pendant and left them for his consort Lady Hulü.
idiomatic: When Bainian was summoned, knowing he could not escape, he cut off his belt-girdle and pendant and left them for his consort Lady Hulü.

literal: He saw the emperor at the Cool Wind Hall in the Xuan Capital Garden; the emperor had Bainian write the character "edict" — it matched what Dezao had submitted — then sent attendants to beat him wildly; others were made to drag Bainian around the hall, beating him as he went; wherever he passed, blood spread across the ground.
idiomatic: He saw the emperor at the Cool Wind Hall in the Xuan Capital Garden; the emperor had Bainian write the character "edict" — it matched what Dezao had submitted — then sent attendants to beat him wildly; others were made to drag Bainian around the hall, beating him as he went; wherever he passed, blood spread across the ground.

literal: When his breath was nearly gone, he said, "Spare my life — I beg to be your uncle's slave.
idiomatic: When his breath was nearly gone, he said, "Spare my life — I beg to be your uncle's slave.

literal: " He was then beheaded and cast into a pool; the pool water turned entirely red; afterward the emperor personally watched as he was buried in the rear garden.
idiomatic: " He was then beheaded and cast into a pool; the pool water turned entirely red; afterward the emperor personally watched as he was buried in the rear garden.

literal: The consort clutched the pendant and wailed, refusing food; after more than a month she too died; the pendant was still in her hand, her fist clenched so it could not be opened; she was fourteen; her father Guang pried it open himself, and only then did it open.
idiomatic: The consort clutched the pendant and wailed, refusing food; after more than a month she too died; the pendant was still in her hand, her fist clenched so it could not be opened; she was fourteen; her father Guang pried it open himself, and only then did it open.

literal: In Houzhu's time the nine courtyards were changed to twenty-seven; when digging they found a small corpse in crimson robe and gold belt — one topknot, one unbound, one foot still in boots.
idiomatic: In the Last Emperor's time the nine courtyards were changed to twenty-seven; when digging they found a small corpse in crimson robe and gold belt — one topknot, one unbound, one foot still in boots.

literal: The palace attendants whispered among themselves that it was Crown Prince Bainian — or some said Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: The palace attendants whispered among themselves that it was Crown Prince Bainian — or some said Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.

literal: An edict made Baize, son of the Prince of Xiangcheng, succeed to the title Prince of Leiling.
idiomatic: An edict made Baize, son of the Prince of Xiangcheng, succeed to the title Prince of Leiling.

literal: When Qi fell he entered the passes, was transferred to Shu, and died there.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered the passes, was transferred to Shu, and died there.

literal: Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang received enfeoffment together with the Prince of Runan, all additionally given Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; later events are unrecorded.
idiomatic: Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang received enfeoffment together with the Prince of Runan, all additionally given honors equal to the three ducal ministers; later events are unrecorded.

literal: The Twelve Princes of Wucheng
idiomatic: The Twelve Princes of Wucheng

literal: Prince Chuo of Nanyang; Prince Yan of Langye; Prince Kuo of Qi'an; Prince Zhen of Beiping
idiomatic: Prince Chuo of Nanyang; Prince Yan of Langye; Prince Kuo of Qi'an; Prince Zhen of Beiping

literal: Prince Renying of Gaoping; Prince Renguang of Huainan; Prince Renji of Xihe; Prince Renyong of Leping
idiomatic: Prince Renying of Gaoping; Prince Renguang of Huainan; Prince Renji of Xihe; Prince Renyong of Leping

literal: Prince Renjian of Yingchuan; Prince Renya of Anyang; Prince Renzhi of Danyang; Prince Renqian of Donghai
idiomatic: Prince Renjian of Yingchuan; Prince Renya of Anyang; Prince Renzhi of Danyang; Prince Renqian of Donghai

literal: Wucheng had thirteen sons: Empress Hu bore Houzhu and Prince Yan of Langye; Lady Li bore Prince Chuo of Nanyang; the rear palace bore Prince Kuo of Qi'an, Prince Zhen of Beiping, Prince Renying of Gaoping, Prince Renguang of Huainan, Prince Renji of Xihe, Prince Renyong of Leping, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan, Prince Renya of Anle, Prince Renzhi of Danyang, and Prince Renqian of Donghai.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan had thirteen sons: Empress Hu bore the Last Emperor and Prince Yan of Langye; Lady Li bore Prince Chuo of Nanyang; the rear palace bore Prince Kuo of Qi'an, Prince Zhen of Beiping, Prince Renying of Gaoping, Prince Renguang of Huainan, Prince Renji of Xihe, Prince Renyong of Leping, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan, Prince Renya of Anle, Prince Renzhi of Danyang, and Prince Renqian of Donghai.

literal: Prince Chuo of Nanyang, styled Rentong, was Wucheng's eldest son.
idiomatic: Prince Chuo of Nanyang, styled Rentong, was Gao Zhan's eldest son.

literal: Born at the fifth hour of the fifth day of the fifth month; only at the noon hour was Houzhu born.
idiomatic: Born at the fifth hour of the fifth day of the fifth month; only at the noon hour was the Last Emperor born.

literal: Wucheng, because Chuo's mother Lady Li was not the legitimate consort, demoted him to second rank; his original name was Rong, styled Junming; he was given in adoption to the Prince of Hanyang.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan, because Chuo's mother Lady Li was not the legitimate consort, demoted him to second rank; his original name was Rong, styled Junming; he was given in adoption to the Prince of Hanyang.

literal: In the third year of Heqing the title was changed to Prince of Nanyang, and a separate heir was established for Hanyang.
idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing the title was changed to Prince of Nanyang, and a separate heir was established for Hanyang.

literal: When Chuo was barely past ten he remained at Jinyang on guard duty.
idiomatic: When Chuo was barely past ten he remained at Jinyang on guard duty.

literal: He loved Persian dogs; Wei Pohuo remonstrated with him; instantly he hacked several dogs to death — their corpses strewn across the ground.
idiomatic: He loved Persian dogs; Wei Pohuo remonstrated with him; instantly he hacked several dogs to death — their corpses strewn across the ground.

literal: Pohuo fled in shock and dared speak no more.
idiomatic: Pohuo fled in shock and dared speak no more.

literal: Later he served as Minister of Works and Governor of Ji Province; he liked to strip people naked, make them crouch in the shape of beasts, and set dogs on them to devour the flesh.
idiomatic: Later he served as minister of works and governor of Ji Province; he liked to strip people naked, make them crouch in the shape of beasts, and set dogs on them to devour the flesh.

literal: Transferred left to Ding Province — he drew well water for a rear pool and from the tower shot at people.
idiomatic: Transferred left to Ding Province — he drew well water for a rear pool and from the tower shot at people.

literal: He loved going about incognito, hunting without limit, indulging in violence at will — saying he was studying Duke Wenxuan's conduct.
idiomatic: He loved going about incognito, hunting without limit, indulging in violence at will — saying he was studying Gao Yang's conduct.

literal: A woman carrying a child was on the road; running to hide in the grass — Chuo snatched her child and fed it to his Persian dog.
idiomatic: A woman carrying a child was on the road; running to hide in the grass — Chuo snatched her child and fed it to his Persian dog.

literal: The woman shrieked and wept; Chuo in anger set the dog on her to eat as well; the dog would not eat; smearing the child's blood on her, then it ate.
idiomatic: The woman shrieked and wept; Chuo in anger set the dog on her to eat as well; the dog would not eat; smearing the child's blood on her, then it ate.

literal: When Houzhu heard of it, he issued an edict to lock Chuo up and send him to the imperial traveling encampment.
idiomatic: When the Last Emperor heard of it, he issued an edict to lock Chuo up and send him to the imperial traveling encampment.

literal: When he arrived, he was pardoned.
idiomatic: When he arrived, he was pardoned.

literal: Asked what at the province gave greatest pleasure, he replied, "Taking many scorpions and mixing them with maggots — watching them is supreme delight.
idiomatic: Asked what at the province gave greatest pleasure, he replied, "Taking many scorpions and mixing them with maggots — watching them is supreme delight.

literal: " That very night Houzhu sent for a peck of scorpions; by dawn he had gathered only two or three sheng; they were placed in a bathing tub and a man was made to lie naked in it, crying out in agony.
idiomatic: " That very night the Last Emperor sent for a peck of scorpions; by dawn he had gathered only two or three sheng; they were placed in a bathing tub and a man was made to lie naked in it, crying out in agony.

literal: The emperor and Chuo watched and laughed without end, saying to Chuo, "Such a delightful sport — why didn't you report it by urgent post earlier?
idiomatic: The emperor and Chuo watched and laughed without end, saying to Chuo, "Such a delightful sport — why didn't you report it by urgent post earlier?

literal: " Chuo on this account came into great favor with Houzhu; he was appointed Grand General and sported with him morning and night.
idiomatic: " Chuo on this account came into great favor with the Last Emperor; he was appointed grand general and sported with him morning and night.

literal: Han Changluan heard of it and had him transferred out as Governor of Qi Province.
idiomatic: Han Changluan heard of it and had him transferred out as governor of Qi Province.

literal: As he was about to depart, Changluan had Chuo's trusted men falsely accuse him of rebellion and memorialized, "This violates the laws of the state and cannot be pardoned.
idiomatic: As he was about to depart, Changluan had Chuo's trusted men falsely accuse him of rebellion and memorialized, "This violates the laws of the state and cannot be pardoned.

literal: " Houzhu could not bear to execute him publicly; he had the favored Hun attendant He Weisa wrestle with Chuo in the rear garden and strangle him to death.
idiomatic: " The Last Emperor could not bear to execute him publicly; he had the favored Hun attendant He Weisa wrestle with Chuo in the rear garden and strangle him to death.
